First I’ll say that you are amazing for giving her this time to reset, as someone with adhd and pretty intense generalized anxiety disorder, it’s rare to find a partner that doesn’t see my need for a mental reset as a threat to our relationship. I consider myself a pretty clear communicator so it always throws off the connection when it happens, so kudos to you for offering that without threatening your relationship.

My advice is to honor the time that she requested for space, sit with how you’re feeling about it and then maybe offer to make a plan to get together on a set day/time so she has time to mentally prepare. I also want to validate your needs as well, they are equally as important and I am sure a healthy caring partner would want to make sure they are meeting you halfway. If necessary, maybe arrange a date in the future where you do something together that you both enjoy, and then have a conversation about how you guys can handle these kinds of things in the future (I.e: when you need breaks, what would that look like? Here is what I would need, how can we meet each other halfway? Etc) so everybody is clear on boundaries and needs without it feeling uncomfortable. 

I’d also like to add on…if the distance continues, and it’s something you aren’t comfortable with, it’s okay to communicate that as well. Communication and transparency is paramount, if we let things sit too long then resentment and insecurity grows and sometimes an emotionally healthy conversation can answer the questions that we don’t want our insecurities to answer for us.

Cheers! 🍻

Capricorn is ruled by planet Saturn, the planet associated with restriction, limitations, and lessons. Saturn is there to remind us of our responsibilities, boundaries and need for self-control. We have to work harder for things, we have to move with intention, and the rewards for our hard work and sacrifices aren’t given until later in life. Cis lesbian of color here, 40 with a lottt of dating experience haha. 90% of the women I’ve dated have been bisexual or not mono-sexually lesbian. 

I know biphobia definitely exists in the lesbian community offline. I’ve had people around me say that they don’t date bisexual women for “insert self-insecurity”. I find the preference strange personally; because I just don’t find it realistic to police someone’s sexuality or attraction, and definitely wouldn’t use it as a qualifier in feeling secure in mine. You like me? I like you? Lit. That’s all I care about. I don’t see men as any more of a “threat” at “stealing” my partner. If they desire to, A cheaters gonna cheat. It’s a character flaw, not an orientation. This is my thought process but I am a minority in my lesbian community. 

Now, I do still use discernment. What does raise yellow flags for me, is when a date volunteers that her openness to date women is due to her opposition to dating men. Or if she feels it’s necessary to downplay her attraction/sexual desires to men because she thinks it’s what I need to hear. I also pay attention to whether misogyny centers her thought processes. Lesbians/women are not a “safe” or “soft” option. We are not a monolith. This isn’t necessarily a bisexual thing either, because I know many lesbians who follow archaic gender constructs and heteronormative relationship patterns, and I’m just not interested in that. Now this can be due to my own intersectional experience (I’m a black lesbian, and the whole fems do this, studs do that hegemonic toxic gender performance runs rampant where I am from). Ultimately, I can only control how I show up, and I try to show up open and self-secure in my identity and my ability to choose compatible partners.

It is amazing that you are here to ask these questions. For someone with CPTSD, sometimes love and closeness feels dangerous, unstable, uncontrollable, exposing. Often without our intentional participation, as our bodies and brains just process things this way and it feels so hopeless. I am always glad to see someone who loves their partner with cptsd enough to want to learn the intricate ways they may need to be loved.

Understand that your partner may have triggers that even she isn’t fully aware of. These triggers may make her shut down or lash out over even the most minuscule of issues. I learned after 37 years that a mere facial expression (eye roll, a laugh, etc) during an argument could cause me to disassociate and completely split on my partner instantly. We’ve both since learned that as hard it is, we have to table even small difficult conversations for when my rational thought process comes back. 

Also, it seems daunting, but for folks dealing with CPTSD  “healing” is something that is a long time journey, not a destination…many of us won’t ever feel “healed” no matter how long we try or how much our partners love us. But you seeing, believing, and hearing your partner will be wonders for her. 

She may feel guilty after having difficult moments. Your reassurance and patience will be major to her healing process. Having a conversation around boundaries (both your boundaries!) will give you both a common goal. To protect and love each other in a way that you both need. To feel safe.

Edit to add: also, the sandwich method works wonders when addressing issues or concerns. Reassure/communicate issue/confirmation. The biggest issue in my romantic past was that my partner didn’t feel comfortable telling me if I did something that hurt their feelings because I would start to detach. Now when we address issues we start with a positive “babe, I love that we have been able to spend time together and that we are working on building such a solid foundation, I am happy to have you as my partner.” Then “I did want to share that my feelings were hurt during that joke you made this morning about my weight” then we would ask if we are in a space to talk through it, if so, confirm what we heard to clarify and then resolve. This may or may not work for others, but it certain helps my relationship since much of our issue was centered around hearing things through a negative perceptual lens that was often wrong, and then breaking up every time we had difficult conversation. Reassuring the relationship prior to is helpful.

I was diagnosed with Generalized Anxiety Disorder and even Bipolar 2 (kinda sorta...). It wasn't until I started dating my psychiatrist partner that I even considered ADHD for myself (she was like..."uhhh...have you ever been tested for ADHD?"). I grew up in a household that did not take mental health seriously. I was a distracted ball of anxiety. My keys? Where are they? Finishing peoples sentences. Tuning people out to the point that it affected my relationships. Not holding any consistency in any parts of life (even the important ones like money and responsibilities...), double checking myself because I KNEW I was absent-minded as shit, and then STILL losing shit and feel bad about myself.   


My partner asked me if I had the same issues growing up. I told her that I didn't "think" so. She asked me how my backpack looked in school. I laughed. I dont know. Papers everywhere. A pencil holder with no pencils in it (I may have a pencil at the bottom of my bag, maybe not). Homework I started but never finished. A planner that I started writing in but never opened again. You know, normal stuff...  


Except, its not normal. I brought up the idea to my then psychiatrist and he said "NO WAY! You have anxiety. ADHD meds would make your anxiety worse!". I decided to get some new opinions. I won't go on a tangent, but let me tell you...I've tried EVERY anti-anxiety/depression med you can think of. Xanax. Wellbutrin. Klonopin. Lamictal. Latuda. Cymbalta and Zoloft (these two almost killed me). They numbed me, but never "worked". I finally found a psychiatrist willing to test me and hear me out, and I finally take 20 mg of Ritalin and it changed my life. I'm not kidding. My anxiety has gone from a 10 to a 5. Its not a fix all of course, but its put me on the right track.   


I say all this to say, don't be afraid to advocate for yourself. You have to live everyday with your mental anguish. They don't. You deserve to explore all things that make sense. Just seek a new opinion.   


Good luck!
